tools.name: search_jobs
tools.description: Search the live job board: postings pulled directly from employers' own hiring systems, 30-day freshness cap. Send job titles, skills and places, never CV text; put the place in location, not in query. Returns slim job cards with the board's parsed pay (salaryMinAnnual/salaryMaxAnnual) and seniority

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Full detail for one job id (from search_jobs), with the complete description and when the board last read the employer's feed. A resumebooster.work/jobs?job=<id> link's id is this argument (and fetch's and apply_myself's). For several ids at once use get_jobs. A dead id answers with what the board k

tools.name: get_jobs
tools.description: Full detail for up to 10 job ids in one call: the shortlist form of get_job. Ids that closed, aged out or were never on this board come back in `unavailable` with the reason, so one dead id never costs the others.

tools.name: check_jobs_open
tools.description: Are these postings still on the board? Up to 50 ids a call with no key, 200 with one: re-verify a saved shortlist before acting on it. Returns open:{id:boolean} and the closed ids, read from the board's index (a closed posting is one the employer's feed stopped listing), not the employer's site at t

tools.description: Help the person apply to one posting themselves, on the employer's own site. tools.name: board_stats
tools.description: Board statistics from a five-minute cache: servable and tracked posting totals, the count of company job boards with open roles (boards, not employers), the category slugs search_jobs takes, and what this connector does not hand on. Answers with no key and is never counted.

tools.name: employer_hiring_record
tools.description: Use this when the person asks how an employer's postings come and go: whether roles come down or sit open, how long they stay open, any recent layoffs filing. It does not judge whether the employer is hiring. Per companyToken (up to 20), as the site prints it: open_roles, tracking_days, feed_total a

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "agent-mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_job, check_jobs_open, apply_myself, search, fetch · Private data: apply_myself, employer_hiring_record · Public sink: search_jobs, apply_myself, employer_hiring_record.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_job, check_jobs_open, apply_myself, search, fetch · Private data: apply_myself, employer_hiring_record · Public sink: search_jobs, apply_myself, employer_hiring_record

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_jobs" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
